claims.summary: Tables, KOT, recipes, QR ordering and menu add-ons, plus the three service-floor workflows that were missing. Reservations refuse to promise one table to two overlapping sittings, free the slot the moment a booking is cancelled, and re-check the clash on every edit; back-to-back seatings are allowed because the intervals are half-open. Staff shifts apply the same overlap rule per person, exclude cancelled shifts from scheduled hours, and report scheduled time explicitly rather than implying hours worked. Kiosk terminals are named and revocable and serve the same catalogue and order path as the table QR, so the room can never hold two menus that disagree.

claims.summary: Location-aware registration scope, blocking warnings and automated multi-GSTIN filing orchestration. One run partitions the invoice register by seller GSTIN, builds GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and the Table 13 document series per registration, and proves the split is lossless by reconciling per-registration totals against the whole register. Invoices carrying no seller GSTIN are quarantined and block the run instead of being spread across registrations or dropped; an empty period and a malformed GSTIN both refuse to report themselves filing-ready.

claims.summary: Warehouse-grade transfer orders support multiple product lines, approval, in-transit reservation, carrier tracking, partial receiving and safe remainder cancellation. Bin locations record placement within a branch as a net-zero map over authoritative location stock, with a derived unplaced remainder, an over-placement report and an explicit reconcile. Bulk repackaging breaks a bulk pack into retail packs conserving base quantity, refusing fractional packs and requiring wastage to be declared. Unattended replenishment executes the branch suggestions on a schedule, disabled by default, capped per run and per transfer, shipping in-transit so a human still receives, and standing down on a re-run because open incoming stock is already subtracted.

claims.summary: Provider-confirmed Razorpay dynamic UPI QR is implemented behind a separate on-demand account capability flag with single-use fixed-amount creation, exact tenant/branch binding, provider polling, signed qr_code.credited handling, mismatch rejection, cancellation and one-bill consumption. The provider-neutral card-terminal lifecycle includes a documented Pine Labs Plutus cloud adapter for bill upload, status polling and cancellation; it pins one terminal to an exact KiranaOS branch, verifies provider paise and acquirer references before confirmation, rejects lookalike production hosts, and passes mocked contract tests. Client request IDs make HTTP retries idempotent. A lost upload response becomes branch-blocking `uncertain` money—not a false failure—and requires an owner-PIN, reasoned provider reconciliation with a unique acquirer reference and atomic audit before it can enter a bill. Production refuses the simulator. Credentialed Pine Labs UAT/physical certification and Ezetap remain outstanding.

competitorEvidence.claim: Pine Labs, Paytm, PhonePe and terminal-linked payments are benchmark integrations.
